targets.title: In vitro pertubations of targets in cancer hallmark processes predict rodent chemical carcinogenesis.
targets.evidence_quote: Our analysis was designed to be an independent assessment of the accuracy and robustness of the 2013 RCCPM (Kleinstreuer et al., 2013).
targets.outcome_computational_quote: We veri ﬁ ed that our software was computing the same odds ratios and con ﬁ dence intervals as the published paper (Kleinstreuer et al. 2013) by checking against the intermediate output ﬁ les pro- vided by Dr. Judson. Thus, we were able to replicate the univariate ORs calculated in the 2013 RCCPM publication.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: The Mann-Whitney-Wilcoxon rank sum test used was not appro- priate for the data due to many tied ranks. Correcting these two chemical classi ﬁ cations and applying a test (Kendall tau-b) that correctly adjusts for ties, we found that the HTS-based cancer hazard scores no longer signi ﬁ cantly predict in vivo cancer results. A change of classi ﬁ cation to a single chemical can change the original study conclusion, which is therefore not robust.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Original data and author-provided code/output were reconstructed independently. Odds ratios and intervals were recovered; permutation discrepancies did not change variable selection, and the one score correction is explicitly minor with no significant impact. Alternative classification and a ties-adjusted test removed significance. The two axes are independent.
